architectural-decision-records.why: records the self-dogfood decision and why the repo hook is not the consumer template
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR 0053: the skills repo arms its own .githooks/pre-push on npm install and runs its own fast offline gates; documents why it is repo-specific (upstream layout, not scripts/ci) and its honest scope/limits
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the hook ships a discriminating test that goes red if it stops blocking
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added test/self-dogfood-prepush.test.mjs: the hook passes when stubbed gates pass and blocks when a stubbed gate fails (two cases); emptying the GATES list would turn the fail cases green
quotes: replace each check with a no-op and require its test to fail

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the change adds an executable hook, so the test level is explicit and registered
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: a fixture-driven test runs the real hook against stub gate scripts; added to the explicit test-file list in package.json so it runs on every Node/shell
quotes: Fast, isolated tests for logic; a smaller number of integration tests for the seams

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: coupling fires on the added hook code; the behavior is pinned as scenarios
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: implements the self-dogfood local pre-flight whose bypass does not escape CI, with discriminating tests for pass and block
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment. Every time this

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the hook spawns processes and install-hooks writes git config
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: the hook runs only a trusted constant list of npm script names (no external input) with shell:true, so there is no command-injection surface; install-hooks never clobbers an existing core.hooksPath and never fails the install
quotes: For the change in front of you, look up the matching sheet in the catalog below

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR and the hook state the scope limit rather than overclaiming
skeptical-audit.what: documented that the hook runs the fast offline gates only, not the full test suite or routing or provenance, that it is a convenience not the authority, and that arming is per-clone and npm-only
quotes: content hash, a query, a version/commit SHA, or a URL + retrieval date;

judge-arch.why: reviewed in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context judge-arch over the hook, the arming wiring, the test, and the ADR before opening the PR
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all

release-deployment-safety.why: a local developer hook armed via the npm prepare lifecycle; nothing deployed, migrated, or released

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: CI/dev tooling; no system, data, or resilience architecture change

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern selected; a run-the-gates loop

sre-operational-readiness.why: no service, SLI/SLO, or alerting change

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal data, retention, or migration

arch-encode.why: dogfood machinery, not a rule encoded from a newly-caught mistake
